commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Unsure (promote pattern): rewrites existing VA pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml (165 lines, net deletions) and removes known-validation-gaps and oracle-coverage-pending entries.
description: cite section 58.1-321 for the no-tax/no-return applicability branch

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix liability rule returned the § 58.1-320 bracket tax unconditionally, with no representation of § 58.1-321(A)'s exemption, so it imposed Virginia tax on individuals the statute exempts (e.g. a single filer with Virginia AGI of $11,000: pre-fix taxable income 11,000 - 8,750 - 930 = 1,320 and tax $26.40, where § 58.1-321 levies none because VAGI is under $11,950).
triage.triage_notes: Only one module file in the commit, so the chunk is complete. Read the pre-fix (06a1cc2e78) and post-fix (623ad4b086) module and both fixture files, and resolved us-va/statute/58.1/58.1-321 through the pinned corpus: § 58.1-321(A) reads 'No tax levied pursuant to § 58.1-320 is imposed, nor any return required to be filed, by: 1. A single individual where the Virginia adjusted gross income ... is less than $11,950 ...' (and $23,900 for an individual and spouse). The pre-fix module listed us-va/statute/58.1/58.1-321 in source_verification.checked_paths and its rationale used it only for the $930 personal exemption, i.e. it claimed to have accounted for 58.1-321 while encoding none of its no-tax rule; the post-fix formula 'if va_pit_pilot_must_file: va_pit_pilot_bracket_tax else: 0' adds that branch. CAVEATS a reviewer should weigh: (1) this is a 'promote' commit that bundles several non-defect changes with the added clause - the derived taxable-income rule (max(0, AGI - supplied deductions - supplied exemptions)) is deleted and replaced by a supplied va_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income boundary, the four bracket floors/rates move from caller-supplied inputs to imports of us-va:statutes/58.1/58/1-320 (a re-grounding that could alternatively be called untraceable_branch), and effective_to '2026-12-31' is added to both rules (could alternatively be called wrong_period_or_effective_date, though bounding a pilot to 2026 is oracle-safety scoping, not something the statute requires). (2) The bracket arithmetic is unchanged in meaning: the old fixtures supply floor_1=0, 3000/5000/17000 and 0.02/0.03/0.05/0.0575, identical to the imported schedule, so no amount changed. (3) The new gate delegates to a caller-supplied boolean rather than encoding § 58.1-321's dollar thresholds, which is why this is a behavioral correction but not a full encoding of the clause. (4) PR #968's body claims the branch was fixed 'to cite section 58.1-321 and add the exact no-tax/no-return condition proof', but the merged content of this commit still cites only 58.1-320 at module level and in the liability proof atom; the 58.1-321 citation and the condition atom with excerpt 'No tax levied pursuant to § 58.1-320 is imposed, nor any return required to be filed' land six minutes later in follow-up commit 0f9550daa 'Cite Virginia no-tax filing threshold', which is citation/provenance-only (mechanical). (5) No PR reviews or review comments were captured in the bundle; the only quoted review finding in the PR body concerns the PR's own new head, not the pre-fix module, which is why confidence sits at 0.55 rather than higher.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute and could not break the substantive core: the pre-fix liability rule was `va_pit_pilot_bracket_tax` with no applicability condition, and the fix changes it to `if va_pit_pilot_must_file: va_pit_pilot_bracket_tax else: 0`, which is a real encoded-meaning change in the direction the first reader describes. The pinned corpus text of § 58.1-321(A) is substantive, not merely procedural — "No tax levied pursuant to § 58.1-320 is imposed, nor any return required to be filed, by: 1. A single individual where the Virginia adjusted gross income ... is less than $11,950" — so the pre-fix module did impose tax the statute exempts (single, VAGI $11,000: 11,000 − 8,750 − 930 = 1,320 taxable, × 2% = $26.40), and it claimed no such carve-out, asserting instead that "the composed liability equals PolicyEngine's before-non-refundable-credits value exactly." Two things do weaken the first reader's case and should be recorded: the quote it used ("cite section 58.1-321 for the no-tax/no-return applicability branch") describes a citation fix made to this PR's own earlier head during its internal review cycle, and the merged module contains no 58.1-321 reference at all (grep for "321" returns nothing; corpus_citation_paths_seen is 58.1-320 ×3), so the clause is delegated to a caller-supplied boolean rather than encoded. The kind still fits — a missing statutory exception is now represented as a condition — but the confidence should sit at moderate, not high, because the gate is entangled with a wholesale boundary rewrite.
triage.verifier_notes:
Quote replacement: drop the pr_body line the first reader used. It refers to a fix applied to an earlier head of PR #968 ("Independent review of the initial exact head found one medium source-fidelity issue: the filing gate cited only section 58.1-320"), i.e. a provenance change to new code inside the PR, and the merged module carries no 58.1-321 citation anywhere (module source_verification collapses to `corpus_citation_path: us-va/statute/58.1/58.1-320`; the new `va_pit_pilot_must_file` input has a prose description and no corpus_citation_path). The decisive evidence is the diff line, not the PR bullet.

This commit is multi-change, not single-defect, and a corpus entry should say so. Besides the applicability gate it: (1) deletes the `va_pit_pilot_taxable_income` rule and replaces the AGI/deduction/exemption chain with a supplied completed-return `va_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income` boundary; (2) re-grounds the bracket schedule from undeclared caller-supplied `va_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor_1..4` / `_rate_1..4` onto seven hashed imports of `us-va:statutes/58.1/58/1-320#...` (a candidate untraceable_branch / re-grounding defect in its own right — the pre-fix rationale openly said "This pipeline supplies those four floors and rates as declared caller-supplied current-authority inputs ... without importing the encoded bracket rules"); (3) adds `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` to both rules where the pre-fix windows were open-ended from 2026-01-01 (a weak wrong_period_or_effective_date candidate — § 58.1-320's rates are not indexed, so the open window was not contrary to source; PR frames it as fail-closed hygiene); (4) adds an `inputs:` block the pre-fix file lacked entirely (the pre-fix file, 118 lines, ends at the liability formula with every supplied variable undeclared).

Corroborating context for the "pre-fix was known-deficient" reading: this commit removes the module's `known-validation-gaps.yaml` `validate_failures` waiver (fingerprint sha256:a79dd05b..., owner @MaxGhenis, issue #782), so the parent state was a waived validate failure, and the `oracle-coverage-pending.yaml` removal is only the deleted `#va_pit_pilot_taxable_income` legal_id. The manifest is `"backend": "manual"` with `"manual_exception": "composition"`, so this is an assembled composition, not encoder output.

Residual doubt for a reviewer (why 0.6 and not 0.8): the dominant motivation in the commit subject and PR summary is oracle re-basing ("replace the supplied-schedule Virginia pilot with the exact completed-return va_taxable_income and va_must_file boundaries"), and the fix does not encode § 58.1-321's thresholds ($11,950 / $23,900, VAGI plus the § 58.1-322.03(5) modification) — it accepts PolicyEngine's va_must_file as a boundary. If the corpus rule is that a clause must be *encoded* to count as "now represented," this shades toward unclear/scope-change; if a newly added applicability condition counts, unrepresented_clause holds. I kept confirmed because the pre-fix module claimed exact equality with the before-credits target and cited 58.1-321 in checked_paths while using it only for the $930 personal exemption, so it did claim the coverage it got wrong.
